name: TCW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: TCW's top belt, 'a prettier piece of gold the industry doesn't have', defended last on the card. Tommy Cornell holds it when the diary opens and through the first ten shows, beating Troy Tornado at Where Angels Fear To Tread and losing to him only by disqualification at Total Mayhem 13. Troy Tornado takes it from Cornell at Excessive Force in June 2008 with the Star Maker, ending Cornell's reign. Troy Tornado keeps it through July 2008, beating Chris Rockwell and Wolf Hawkins in a three-way match at Summer Showdown with the Star Maker. Troy Tornado keeps it through August 2008: at Hotter Than Hell he beats Brent Hill and Wolf Hawkins in a three-way match, pinning Hawkins after the Star Maker. Troy Tornado is still champion at the end of September 2008: he beats Tyson Baine, Sammy Bach in a ladder match and Chris Rockwell and Eddie Peak, and at Destructive Energy, in a three-way match with Johnny Bloodstone and Tommy Cornell, he and Bloodstone together make Cornell submit; the match ends with both men celebrating, Mayhem Midden saying he will have to talk to the Board, and the commentary saying only that Cornell is not the World Heavyweight Champion. The diary now shows two belts in October 2008: Tommy Cornell walks off with the belt Mayhem Midden is carrying, the Board bars him from title matches for six months, and Troy Tornado and Johnny Bloodstone each appear with a new custom belt, the prediction key billing Tornado as the Standing Champion and Bloodstone as champion of the Canadian Belt. At Crunch Time Tornado keeps his belt, beating Jeremy Stone and Remo Richardson in a three-way match with the Star Maker, and Bloodstone keeps the Canadian Belt, beating Brent Hill with the Bloodstone Mutilation. The Board recognises both belts as championships in November 2008: Mayhem Midden announces that Troy Tornado's and Johnny Bloodstone's belts are recognised, with the proviso that TCW cannot have two World Heavyweight Champions, and orders the two men, or whoever has beaten them for a belt in the meantime, to meet in the Malice in Wonderland main event in January to unify the belts. At A Little South Of Sanity Tornado, barring Tommy Cornell from a title shot, beats him in a non-title match with the Star Maker, and Bloodstone keeps the Canadian Belt, beating Chris Rockwell in a half-hour match. The two belts stay apart through December 2008, the Board's edict that they be unified at Malice in Wonderland in January standing: Johnny Bloodstone keeps the Canadian Belt, beating Edd Stone and, in a non-title match, Merle O'Curle, and Troy Tornado, as Triple-Threat Champion, picks the men for a six-man match whose winner takes the third place in his defence. At Psycho Circus, after Tommy Cornell hits Tornado and Eddie Peak with the retired TCW belt, Tornado beats Peak and Jeremy Stone in a three-way match with the Star Maker, and the diary's preview makes the winner of that match the man who goes on to face Bloodstone at Malice in Wonderland to unify the belts.

name: TCW International Championship
epitaph: The belt of the middle of the card. Wolf Hawkins holds it when the diary opens, keeps it against Koshiro Ino at Where Angels Fear To Tread by interference, and loses it to Ino in a no-disqualification match at Total Mayhem 13. Ino keeps it through June 2008, beating Sam Keith on Total Wrestling in Week 2 and, at Excessive Force, losing to Chris Rockwell only by disqualification. Ino keeps it through July 2008: Tommy Cornell's win on Total Wrestling comes only by disqualification, and at Summer Showdown Ino beats Sammy Bach with the Kobra's Bite. Ino keeps it through August 2008 until Hotter Than Hell, where John Anderson beats him with the Ammo Dump and the diary says TCW has a new International Champion. Anderson keeps it through September 2008: Wolf Hawkins beats him only by count out, and he beats Frankie Perez, Acid and, at Destructive Energy, Eric Tyler, each with the Ammo Dump. Anderson keeps it through October 2008: he draws with Sean Deeley on Total Wrestling when time runs out and beats Jack Marlowe with the Ammo Dump. At Crunch Time he makes an open challenge and Sean Deeley beats him by count-out, a result the diary does not treat as a change of champion. Anderson keeps it through November 2008: he beats Texas Pete on Total Wrestling after Wolf Hawkins interferes, and at A Little South Of Sanity he beats Pete and Hawkins in a three-way match, pinning Hawkins with the Ammo Dump after the Enforcers have beaten him down. Anderson keeps it through December 2008: he beats American Buffalo after Wolf Hawkins's Full Moon Rising lands on the Buffalo, draws with Hawkins at the time limit on Total Wrestling and at Psycho Circus beats Hawkins in a match the diary rates an A, with the Ammo Dump after fifteen minutes.

name: TCW All Action Championship
epitaph: The belt the narrator wants to turn into a test of a rising wrestler, with the weight limit removed. Sammy Bach holds it when the diary opens and loses it at Total Mayhem 13 to the Syndicate's Edd Stone. Edd Stone defends it at Excessive Force in June 2008 in the Hangtime Match of his own devising, against Sammy Bach and Acid, and keeps it. Edd Stone keeps it through July 2008, beating Hell Monkey at Summer Showdown with the Party's Over; Hell Monkey won the shot in a three-way ladder match on Badge of Honor. Edd Stone keeps it through August 2008: Art Reed, the fans' choice in a web poll, beats him at Hotter Than Hell only by count out, so the title stays with Stone. Edd Stone keeps it through September 2008: he beats the Cannonball Kid on Badge of Honor, when the Kid tries a powerbomb, and Art Reed in the rematch at Destructive Energy. Edd Stone loses it at Crunch Time in October 2008: Frankie Perez, who won the number one contendership in a three-way match on Badge of Honor, beats him with the P-Clutch after a mule kick to the head, taking his first TCW gold. Frankie Perez keeps it in his first month with it: at A Little South Of Sanity, after entrants chosen on Badge of Honor, he beats Art Reed, Greg Keith and Freddy Huggins in a four-way match, Greg Keith tapping to the P-Clutch. Frankie Perez keeps it through December 2008, beating Hell Monkey, who wins the ladder match for the contract, with the P-Clutch at Psycho Circus after Perez has abandoned Chris Rockwell and allied with Remo Richardson and Phil Vibert.

name: TCW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The pair of belts the Machines hold when the diary opens, for a full year by May 2008. They retain against Painful Procedure at Where Angels Fear To Tread and against the Young Guns at Total Mayhem 13. The Machines lose the belts to the New Wave at Excessive Force in June 2008. The New Wave keep the belts through July 2008, beating the Young Guns at Summer Showdown with the Special Force, after losing a non-title match to the School of Tradition on Badge of Honor. The New Wave keep the belts through August 2008, beating the Easy Riders, the British Lions and, at Hotter Than Hell, the School of Tradition. The New Wave keep the belts through September 2008: a disqualification loss to Freddy Huggins and Sammy Bach does not cost them the titles, and they beat the Keith Brothers on Total Wrestling, the Enforcers on Badge of Honor and, at Destructive Energy, the School of Tradition with Scout's Special Force. The New Wave keep the belts through October 2008, the Stone Brothers drawing with them in a non-title match on Total Wrestling; at Crunch Time they beat the Easy Riders, the tournament winners, only by disqualification. The New Wave keep the belts through November 2008, beating the Elite Express and the British Lions and drawing with the Keith Brothers on Total Wrestling when the Easy Riders interfere; at A Little South Of Sanity they beat the Easy Riders and the Stone Brothers in a three-team elimination match. The New Wave keep the belts through December 2008 until Psycho Circus, where they lose them in a hardcore match to the Easy Riders: Billy Fonda and Peter Hopper beat down Scout, take him to the corner and loop a chain, which Carl Batch holds, round his neck to anchor him to the turnbuckle, and finish Guide with the Emergency Stop onto a steel chair. The diary's closing notes call the fall of the New Wave a long reign ended and doubt that the Easy Riders will hold the belts as long.

name: TCW Hard Hitting Championship
epitaph: TCW's newest belt: Mayhem Midden unveils it on Total Wrestling in Week 2 June 2008 and makes every match for it No Holds Barred (no run-ins, no weapons, no disqualification for using only your body). Eddie Peak, Sam Keith, Tyson Baine (who beats American Buffalo in a Strap Match) and Ricky Dale Johnson (who beats Frankie Perez on Badge of Honor) qualify, and Sam Keith wins the first championship in a four-way match at Excessive Force. Sam Keith keeps it through July 2008: he wins by disqualification over Tyson Baine on Total Wrestling, after Tommy Cornell's chair, and beats Ricky Dale Johnson at Summer Showdown with the Proton Lock. Sam Keith keeps it through August 2008: he beats Sammy Bach on Total Wrestling and, in a No Holds Barred match at Hotter Than Hell, Tommy Cornell. Sam Keith keeps it through September 2008: he draws with Chris Rockwell on Total Wrestling when the time limit runs out and, in a No Holds Barred match at Destructive Energy, beats Jeremy Stone with the Proton Lock. Sam Keith keeps it through November 2008, beating JD Morgan with the Proton Lock on Total Wrestling before Sammy Bach, who has taken Wolf Hawkins' contendership as a favour, hits him with a chair; at A Little South Of Sanity he beats Bach with the NeutronPlex. Sam Keith keeps it through December 2008: at Psycho Circus, in a No Holds Barred match, Sammy Bach wins by disqualification when Texas Pete hits him with a chair, a result the diary does not treat as a title change.
